  • src/ui/client/Workspace.tsx — UserLinksPage
  • src/ui/api.ts — GET /user-links, PUT/DELETE /user-links/:planeUserId
  • src/ui/mapping-check.ts — createGithubUserLookup, createPlaneMemberCheck
  • src/app/identity.ts — email matching
  • src/db/ledgers.ts — user-link tombstones

28 · Sync health and the audit log

You will get questions like “why didn’t my PR move WEB-42?” or “is the integration working at all?”. Answer them with two tools:

  • Sync health — a quick status board per mapping.
  • Audit log — a diary of every delivery git-sync received and every decision it made.

This chapter explains both, for workspace admins and for the instance admin.

Three levels of “healthy”

Level Where Proves
Liveness GET /git-sync/healthz → {"status":"ok"} The HTTP service answers. Nothing about the database, GitHub or Plane.
Instance health God mode → Connection health and Setup checks (chapter 23) Database reachable, credentials decryptable, App registered correctly, deliveries seen
Mapping health Workspace → Mapped repositories → Sync health This repository’s deliveries, writes, errors, rate limits

Sync health cards

Each row in Mapped repositories has a Sync health card. The page refreshes it every 30 seconds; Refresh sync health refreshes it now.

Line Meaning Worry when
Last GitHub delivery Newest verified GitHub webhook for this repository never, or hours old while people are pushing
Last Plane delivery Newest verified Plane webhook for this workspace never, or old while people edit work items (see the banner below)
Last successful write Newest write git-sync completed to Plane or GitHub for this mapping Deliveries are recent but writes are not
Errors in the last 24 hours Count of failed audit entries for this mapping; the number links to the audit log filtered to them Not zero — open it
Rate-limited until Shown only while GitHub or Plane has paused git-sync; writes resume at that time Often, or far in the future
Disabled · reason Shown only when the mapping cannot sync Always — fix the reason

Banners at the top of the workspace page

Banner Meaning Do
“The sync database is unreachable. Settings and activity cannot be loaded.” git-sync cannot reach its Postgres Operator: check plane-db and git-sync logs
“Plane changes have stopped arriving. Ask a workspace admin to re-enable the Git sync webhook in Plane’s webhook settings.” Reconciliation found Plane changes newer than the last Plane delivery by more than 30 minutes. Plane has probably switched the webhook off. Re-enable it (chapter 29)
“GitHub App credentials could not be decrypted. Ask an instance admin to repair the GitHub App settings.” Stored secrets unreadable Chapter 30

The audit log

Open Audit log in the workspace tabs (/git-sync/ui/workspaces/<slug>/audit). Entries are newest first.

Column Content
When Time recorded
Event A readable label plus “· GitHub” or “· Plane” for the source
Outcome What happened: handled, applied, registered, retained, ignored, failed, partial, fired, created, service_identity, …
Detail Short summary: the error text if any, otherwise “GitHub account: login”, “Rule: name” or “Recorded sync activity”; Show raw expands the full entry

Buttons per entry:

Button On Effect
Show raw Every entry Expands the stored JSON detail (payload excerpts, ids, error)
Replay Received deliveries (Webhook received) Asks “Replay this delivery? It runs again under a new delivery id and may write to Plane and GitHub.” and queues the stored payload again
Retry / Retry scheduled Sync write failed entries Schedules that failed write again (chapter 29)

Load older entries pages further back.

Warning: Raw entries can contain issue text, comments and GitHub logins. Keep screenshots of them private.

Common event labels

Label Meaning
Webhook received A verified delivery was accepted (raw kind inbound_delivery)
Branch or commit push / Pull request updated / GitHub issue updated / Plane work item updated / Comment updated / Commit status updated Processing of that kind of event
Smart Commit action completed One Smart Commit command was applied
Automation rule matched A rule matched: applied (wrote), ignored (matched but every target was skipped by tier or merge guard), failed (e.g. unknown state)
Pull request ready to merge Ready-for-merge fired for a head commit
Work item creation requested by pull request A WEB-NEW PR created an item
Mirrored work item created Issue mirroring created a partner
Work item reference not found A key in a PR matched nothing
Service account attribution The sender was unlinked or a bot, or had no stored token, so the service identity was used
Account matched by email Automatic user link (chapter 27)
Sync write / Sync write failed / Sync write retry scheduled Outbox write results
GitHub installation is not approved / GitHub installation access removed Mapping authority problems
Plane webhook has stopped arriving The silent-webhook detector fired
Development link updated / Deployment status updated Development panel data changed

Filtering

The page has no filter controls. Filters are URL parameters, and the health links set them for you:

Parameter Example Shows
errors=1 /git-sync/ui/workspaces/acme/audit?errors=1 Failed entries only
mappingId=<id> …/audit?mappingId=1&errors=1 One mapping
hours=<n> …/audit?errors=1&hours=24&mappingId=1 The last n hours (up to 8760)

The Errors in the last 24 hours number opens ?mappingId=<id>&errors=1&hours=24, and the page says “Errors in the last 24 hours for mapping id.”

The other URL parameters work the same way. For example, ?mappingId=1&hours=24 shows one mapping’s last day:

Reading a story from the audit log

Real entries from the demo run, oldest first, for one push to WEB-42’s branch:

Entry (Event column) Outcome Meaning
Smart commit source retained The commit was recorded for processing
Service account attribution service_identity alex-dev is linked, but no Plane token is stored, so Plane writes use the bot
Smart commit target / Smart commit command / Smart commit step retained / registered #comment for WEB-42 was turned into a durable write
Smart commit registered All commands of the commit are registered
Webhook received handled The push delivery itself (recorded when processing ends)
Smart Commit action completed applied The comment was written in Plane
Automation rule matched (Show raw: "rule": "default: branch_pushed") applied WEB-42 moved to In Progress

Kinds without a friendly label are shown with their internal name made readable, for example smart_commit_failed → “Smart commit failed”.

Instance audit (God mode)

God mode → GitHub Sync → Instance audit (/git-sync/ui/admin/audit) shows activity across the instance:

  • By default: “Showing activity with no workspace.” These are deliveries that could not be tied to a workspace, such as installation events, unmapped repositories and signature problems.
  • With ?scope=all: “Showing instance and workspace activity.” — every workspace, with a Workspace column and View workspace activity links.
  • The Failures in the last 24 hours link in Connection health opens it filtered to errors.

Without ?scope=all the instance audit shows only activity that belongs to no workspace:

What to send when asking for help

When a developer reports a problem (chapter 17 tells them what to collect), gather:

  1. The work item key, the PR / commit link, and the time.
  2. The mapping’s health card (screenshot without raw data).
  3. The audit entries around that time, with Show raw expanded, shared privately.
  4. God mode Setup checks results.
  5. For operators: docker compose … logs --tail 200 git-sync, with secrets removed.

What you learned

  • /healthz proves liveness only; use God mode checks and per-mapping health cards for real status.
  • Health cards show last deliveries, last write, 24-hour errors, and, only when relevant, Rate-limited until and Disabled.
  • The audit log explains every decision. Show raw reveals details, Replay re-runs a delivery, Retry re-runs a failed write.
  • Filters are URL parameters (errors, mappingId, hours, scope=all); there are no on-page filter controls.

29 · Operations: update, rotate, replay, back up, uninstall

This chapter is the operator’s runbook. All commands run on the Plane server, in your Plane directory, with the filenames your deployment uses. Wherever you see docker compose …, use the full start command the installer printed (both Compose files and the env file), for example:

cd /root/plane && docker compose -f docker-compose.yaml -f docker-compose.override.yaml --env-file plane.env up -d

Daily checks

Check How Good
Service alive curl -i https://plane.example.com/git-sync/healthz 200 {"status":"ok"}
Container healthy docker compose … ps git-sync healthy
Recent logs docker compose … logs --tail 100 git-sync No repeated errors
Instance status God mode → GitHub Sync → Connection health, Setup checks Database reachable, checks Verified
Per-repository status Workspace → Mapped repositories health cards Recent deliveries, few errors

Update git-sync

Goal: run a newer git-sync, keeping all settings and data

Before you start: back up (below). Write down the exact installer options this deployment uses (--plane-dir, --env-file, --proxy external --gateway-network …, --keep-plane-ui).

Steps

  1. Enter the checkout and pull:
cd ~/git-sync
git pull
  1. Re-run the installer with the same options:
sudo ./install.sh --plane-dir /root/plane          # plus your other options
  1. Check /git-sync/healthz, God mode Setup checks and a mapping’s health card.

Result:

  • The image git-sync:local is rebuilt and the service restarted.
  • Database migrations run automatically on start; they are ordered, recorded, and safe with several replicas.
  • git-sync.env, GITSYNC_TOKEN_KEY, the database and stored secrets are kept. The installer does not ask for the Plane secrets again.

If it went wrong:

  • Keep the previous checkout revision, and the previous image if you tagged it. To roll back, check out the old revision and re-run the installer.
  • A schema-incompatible rollback needs the database backup taken before the update: there are no down-migrations.
  • Existing Plane UI fork images are reused, not rebuilt. If a release changes the fork patches, remove the old plane-frontend-gitsync:v1.4.2 / plane-admin-gitsync:v1.4.2 images before re-running, so they are rebuilt.

Note: “Change a setting” uses the same command: re-run ./install.sh with the new option, for example --public-url. Existing values are kept unless you supply new ones.

Upgrading Plane itself

The UI fork is pinned to Plane v1.4.2. If you upgrade Plane:

  1. The installer keeps Plane’s stock UI automatically for versions it does not recognize. git-sync keeps working; use the direct /git-sync/ui/… links.
  2. To get the menus back, the fork’s eight files must be re-applied and rebuilt for the new release (see apps/README.md, scripts/verify-fork-patch.mjs).
  3. Always start Plane with the installer’s printed command, not Plane’s setup.sh, so the override (and git-sync) is included.

Rotate the bot’s Plane API key

Goal: replace PLANE_SERVICE_PAT without downtime

Steps

  1. Signed in as the bot, create a new Personal Access Token (chapter 21, step 2).
  2. Re-run the installer with the new key in the environment, without putting it in your shell history:
read -r -s -p 'New bot PAT: ' GITSYNC_PLANE_PAT
export GITSYNC_PLANE_PAT
sudo --preserve-env=GITSYNC_PLANE_PAT ./install.sh --plane-dir /root/plane
unset GITSYNC_PLANE_PAT

(On rootless Docker, run without sudo as the user who owns Plane.) 3. The installer verifies the key with Plane, writes it and the bot’s user ID to git-sync.env, and restarts git-sync. 4. Revoke the old token in Plane after checking that writes still work (make a test Smart Commit or edit a mirrored issue).

If the stored key was revoked first, an interactive re-run prints “Plane rejected the API key” and asks for a new one.

Warning: Never change GITSYNC_TOKEN_KEY when rotating the PAT. It is the encryption key for stored secrets, not a Plane credential.

Rotate the Plane webhook secret

git-sync accepts the current secret and, during a rotation, one previous secret.

  1. Note the current value of PLANE_WEBHOOK_SECRET in git-sync.env.
  2. In Plane: Workspace settings → Webhooks → the git-sync webhook → regenerate the secret key. Copy it.
  1. In git-sync.env set PLANE_WEBHOOK_SECRET=<new> and PLANE_WEBHOOK_SECRET_PREVIOUS=<old>. Then run docker compose … up -d git-sync.
  2. After an hour, delete PLANE_WEBHOOK_SECRET_PREVIOUS and run up -d git-sync again.

Keep the gap between steps 2 and 3 short, at a quiet time. A Plane delivery that matches neither secret is refused with 401, and Plane never resends it.

Rotate GitHub App credentials

Credential How
Private key GitHub: Generate a private key. God mode: paste it into Private key (PEM), leave other secrets empty, Save GitHub App. Then delete the old key on GitHub.
Client secret GitHub: generate a new one. God mode: OAuth client secret → Save GitHub App. Delete the old one on GitHub.
Webhook secret Change it on GitHub and in God mode Webhook secret close together. There is no “previous” GitHub secret, so deliveries signed with the other secret in between fail with 401; redeliver them (below).

New credentials are used within about five seconds of saving; no restart is needed.

The encryption key (GITSYNC_TOKEN_KEY)

  • It encrypts the App’s private key, webhook secret and client secret, members’ GitHub tokens, and in-flight OAuth verifiers.
  • It must decode to exactly 32 bytes. The installer generates it once and always keeps it.
  • Do not rotate it. There is no re-encryption command. With a different key, every stored secret becomes unreadable: God mode shows GitHub App credentials cannot be decrypted. Save the App secrets again., GitHub webhooks get 503, and members must reconnect.
  • If the key was lost, chapter 30 explains recovery: restore the key, or re-enter every secret.

Redeliver GitHub webhooks

GitHub does not retry a delivery that received an error. After any outage (git-sync down, 503 while secrets were unreadable, 401 during a secret change):

  1. GitHub → Settings → Developer settings → GitHub Apps → your App → Advanced → Recent deliveries.
  1. Redeliver every delivery marked failed since the problem began.

Redelivery is safe: git-sync deduplicates by delivery id, and writes are idempotent.

Replay a delivery from the audit log

If a delivery did reach git-sync but was processed wrongly (for example, before you fixed a missing state or a rule), a workspace admin can replay it:

  1. Audit log → find the Webhook received entry.
  2. Replay → confirm “Replay this delivery? It runs again under a new delivery id and may write to Plane and GitHub.”
  3. The entry Webhook replay requested appears, followed by the new processing.

Writes that already succeeded are recognized and not repeated. Only deliveries whose raw payload is still retained (audit payload retention: 90 days) can be replayed.

Retry a failed write

When an outbound write failed permanently (for example a permission was missing, or a state was deleted), fix the cause and then:

  1. Audit log → open errors (?errors=1) → the Sync write failed entry.
  2. Select Retry. It changes to Retry scheduled.

The retry re-checks the mapping’s authority first. A write whose installation has since been revoked is still refused. A write that is merely rate-limited retries by itself at the deadline; leave it alone.

Re-enable a Plane webhook that Plane switched off

Plane v1.4.2 switches a webhook off after about 5 failed connection attempts over 30–50 minutes, and emails its creator. git-sync notices with the next reconciliation (default every 60 minutes). It audits Plane webhook has stopped arriving and shows the banner “Plane changes have stopped arriving…”.

  1. Fix what made git-sync unreachable; check /git-sync/healthz.
  2. Plane: Workspace settings → Webhooks → the git-sync webhook → switch it on.
  3. Changes made while it was off are not resent. Re-save the affected work items in Plane (or make the matching change on GitHub). The audit entry’s latestChangeAt and lastDeliveryAt show the gap.

When Valkey alone is down, Plane deliveries are kept in Postgres and replayed every minute once it is back, so nothing is lost. If both Valkey and Postgres are down, Plane deliveries get 503 and are lost.

Backups

Back these up together:

What Where
The gitsync database Plane’s Postgres: docker compose … exec -T plane-db pg_dump -U <plane superuser> gitsync > gitsync.sql
git-sync.env (contains GITSYNC_TOKEN_KEY and secrets) Plane’s directory, mode 0600
git-sync/ directory (App key file, credential-state marker) Plane’s directory
What Where
docker-compose.override.yaml and any external proxy config Plane’s directory / your proxy

Warning: A database backup without the matching GITSYNC_TOKEN_KEY cannot decrypt its secrets. Store them together, privately. The installer’s .bak-<time> files also contain secrets.

Take the backup at a quiet time, or stop git-sync briefly (docker compose … stop git-sync). Valkey jobs are not in the database; note the backup time, so that after a restore you know which GitHub deliveries to redeliver.

Uninstall

Goal: remove git-sync and keep its data

sudo ./install.sh --uninstall          # add --plane-dir/--env-file as used at install

This removes the git-sync service and the installer-managed override entries and proxy route. It restarts Plane’s proxy and apps without git-sync (“Restarting Plane’s proxy and apps without git-sync”). The gitsync database, git-sync.env and the git-sync/ directory are kept, so a later install picks everything up again.

Goal: remove git-sync and delete its data

sudo ./install.sh --uninstall --purge

The installer asks “Delete git-sync’s database, settings and stored GitHub credentials for good? [y/N]”.

  • Deleted: the gitsync database and role, git-sync.env and the state directory.
  • Not deleted: Plane’s database, Plane’s data, and the timestamped .bak- files, which still contain secrets. Delete those yourself.

After either form:

  • Remove any route you added to an external proxy yourself.
  • Uninstall the GitHub App from your organizations on GitHub if you no longer need it.
  • Delete the Plane webhook in Workspace settings → Webhooks.
  • Revoke the bot’s API key.

What you learned

  • Update with git pull and the same ./install.sh options; settings, secrets and the encryption key are kept.
  • Rotate the bot PAT through the installer, and the Plane webhook secret with the _PREVIOUS overlap. Rotate App secrets in God mode. Never rotate GITSYNC_TOKEN_KEY.
  • Use GitHub Recent deliveries for failed GitHub webhooks, Replay for deliveries that arrived, and Retry for failed writes.
  • Back up the database, git-sync.env and git-sync/ together. --uninstall keeps data; --purge deletes git-sync’s data only.

Source files

  • install.sh, src/install/env-file.ts, src/install/main.ts — update, rotation, uninstall
  • deploy/APPLY.md — sections 9–12
  • src/operations/tooling.ts, src/operations/outbox.ts — replay and retry
  • src/sync/reconcile.ts, src/queue/cron.ts — silent-webhook detection, spool replay
  • src/index.ts — /git-sync/healthz

30 · Admin troubleshooting

Start from the symptom, then check the smallest part that could cause it. Reinstalling rarely fixes a wrong callback URL or a wrong account. Before you change anything, collect the evidence that chapter 28 lists (health card, audit entries, setup checks, logs).

A quick triage order

  1. curl -i https://<plane>/git-sync/healthz — is the service up?
  2. God mode → Connection health and Setup checks — database, credentials, App registration, deliveries.
  3. Workspace → the mapping’s Sync health card — deliveries arriving? Disabled? Rate-limited until?
  4. Workspace → Audit log (?errors=1) — what did git-sync decide and why?
  5. docker compose … logs --tail 200 git-sync — startup and connection errors.

Installation and pages

Symptom Likely cause Fix
Installer errors — See chapter 21, “Troubleshooting the installer”
GitHub Sync page inside Plane is blank Proxy adds X-Frame-Options: DENY or frame-ancestors 'none' to /git-sync/* Exclude /git-sync/* from the header in every proxy layer (chapter 21, step 6)
GitHub Sync missing from Plane menus Stock UI kept (--keep-plane-ui or non-v1.4.2 Plane), or Plane was started with setup.sh Use direct links; start Plane with the installer’s printed command
Members ask where GitHub Sync is It is admin-only in Workspace settings Send them /git-sync/ui/workspaces/<slug>/account
Not authorised on /git-sync/ui/admin No God mode session in this browser Sign in to God mode, reload
Not authorised “Workspace settings need a workspace admin.” You are a member, not an admin Ask an admin, or use My GitHub account
404 for every /git-sync/ URL Proxy route missing (external proxy) or git-sync not running Add handle /git-sync/* { reverse_proxy git-sync:3100 } before the Plane route; check the container
409 “This workspace address belonged to a Plane workspace that was deleted. An instance admin must remove its old git-sync data before it can be used again.” A new workspace reuses a deleted workspace’s slug Instance admin: on the God mode page, open the browser console and run fetch('/git-sync/api/instance/workspaces/<slug>/stale-data', {method: 'DELETE'}) (API only, no button). This deletes git-sync’s old data for that slug after checking the live workspace.

Symptom Likely cause Fix
redirect_uri is not associated with this application on GitHub Callback URL or Client ID wrong Callback must be <PUBLIC_ORIGIN>/git-sync/oauth/github/callback; use the App’s Client ID
Connect GitHub disabled: “Ask the instance admin to configure the GitHub App client ID, client secret and App slug.” Missing slug/Client ID/secret Complete GitHub App in God mode

Credentials cannot be decrypted

Goal: restore working credentials after a key mismatch

Option A — you still have the right key (best):

  1. Find the GITSYNC_TOKEN_KEY that matches the database, for example in a backup of git-sync.env or an installer .bak- file.
  2. Put it back in git-sync.env and run docker compose … up -d git-sync.
  3. Check setup again, then redeliver failed GitHub deliveries (chapter 29).

Option B — the key is lost:

  1. In God mode → GitHub App, re-enter every secret: Private key (PEM), Webhook secret and OAuth client secret. Generate a new private key and client secret on GitHub if you do not have them. Save GitHub App.
  2. Every member must Reconnect on My GitHub account; their old tokens cannot be read.
  3. Redeliver failed GitHub deliveries.

Symptom Likely cause Fix

Asking for help

Share, privately:

  • the Plane version and git-sync commit (git rev-parse --short HEAD in the checkout);
  • the non-secret installer options;
  • the God mode Setup checks results;
  • the failing page;
  • relevant audit entries;
  • log lines with secrets removed.

Never share git-sync.env, .bak- files, raw tokens or the PEM. Do not run the installer with bash -x: it prints secrets.

What you learned

  • Triage in order: healthz → God mode checks → health card → audit log → logs.
  • Most failures are configuration: proxy framing, callback URLs, the nine events, one-installation-per-workspace, direction and policies, and the merge rule’s base branch.
  • A key mismatch is fixed by restoring the matching GITSYNC_TOKEN_KEY, or by re-entering every secret and asking members to reconnect.
  • The signed-commit checkbox is not enforced; use the environment variable.

Appendix A · All routes

Every address the git-sync service answers lives under /git-sync, on the same origin as Plane. The reverse proxy that serves Plane forwards /git-sync/* to the git-sync container on port 3100. In this appendix, <slug> is the workspace slug (for example acme), and the IDs are Plane IDs.

Who may call:

  • Member: any signed-in Plane member of that workspace (Plane web session cookie).
  • Workspace admin: Plane workspace role Admin.
  • Instance admin: a Plane God mode session.
  • Signed: requests verified with an HMAC signature, no cookie.
  • Anyone: no authentication.

Every call that changes something (POST, PUT, PATCH, DELETE) must also carry the service’s own Origin, so cross-site requests are refused.

Address Page Who may open it
/git-sync/ui/workspaces/<slug> Git sync: <slug>, Repositories tab (connection, mapped repositories, map a repository) Workspace admin
/git-sync/ui/workspaces/<slug>/mappings/<id> Mapping Settings Workspace admin
/git-sync/ui/workspaces/<slug>/mappings/<id>/policies Mapping Conflict policies Workspace admin
/git-sync/ui/workspaces/<slug>/mappings/<id>/rules Mapping Rules Workspace admin
/git-sync/ui/workspaces/<slug>/mappings/<id>/dry-run Mapping Test rules Workspace admin

Appendix B · Settings and environment variables

git-sync keeps its configuration in three places:

  1. Environment variables in git-sync.env. The installer writes this file next to Plane’s own plane.env, and it is read when the container starts.
  2. Instance settings that an instance admin edits in God mode.
  3. Mapping settings that a workspace admin edits per repository.

Environment variables (src/config/env.ts)

Changing an environment variable takes effect only after the git-sync container restarts.

Variable Required Default Meaning
DATABASE_URL yes — PostgreSQL connection for git-sync’s own schema (the installer reuses Plane’s Postgres server)
REDIS_URL yes — Valkey/Redis for the job queues (Plane’s Valkey)
QUEUE_PREFIX no gitsync Prefix of the queue keys
PORT / HOST no 3100 / 0.0.0.0 Where the service listens
PLANE_BASE_URL yes — Plane’s API as seen from the container (internal address)
PLANE_SERVICE_PAT yes — API key of the bot service account in Plane
Variable Required Default Meaning
PLANE_SERVICE_USER_ID yes — Plane user ID of that bot; its own changes are recognized and not echoed back
PLANE_WEBHOOK_SECRET yes — Secret of the Plane workspace webhook
PLANE_WEBHOOK_SECRET_PREVIOUS no — Old Plane webhook secret, still accepted while you rotate it
PLANE_SESSION_COOKIE_NAME no session-id Must match Plane’s SESSION_COOKIE_NAME
PLANE_API_RATE_PER_MINUTE no 60 Requests per minute git-sync may send to Plane; must equal Plane’s API_KEY_RATE_LIMIT

Appendix C · Reference, magic-word and Smart Commit grammar

Every table in this appendix is generated. manual/scripts/grammar-tables.mjs runs each example through the real parsers in src/parse/references.ts and src/github/smart-commits.ts, then writes the result here. The tables are rebuilt with every manual build, so they always match the code. The examples come from tests/parse/references.test.ts, tests/github/smart-commits.test.ts, tests/a8/grammar.test.ts and the chapters of this manual.

Work-item keys

A key is a project prefix, a hyphen and a number: WEB-42, API2-103. The prefix starts with a letter, followed by 1–11 letters or digits, so it is 2–12 characters long. The key must not be glued to letters or digits on either side, and no _ may follow the number. Leading zeros are dropped, so WEB-0042 is WEB-42. A recognized key still has to exist in Plane: git-sync looks it up, and an unknown key is ignored and written to the audit log.

Prefixes that are never read as work-item keys (NOT_PROJECTS in src/parse/references.ts): UTF, SHA, ISO, AES, RSA, CVE, CWE, RFC, TLS, SSL, MD, ES, PEP, USB, HTTP, IPV, SSH, GPT, RS, CRC, UTC, WIN.

Where git-sync looks, and what a bare key means

Place Case of a bare key Tier of a bare key Tier after a magic word
Pull request head branch any case closing the word’s tier
Pull request title UPPERCASE only closing the word’s tier
Pull request body UPPERCASE only relation the word’s tier
Commit message (push rules only) UPPERCASE only relation the word’s tier

A key that follows a magic word may be in any case. The pull request handler reads only the branch, title and body. Commit messages never link a pull request; they are read only by Smart Commits and by push / commit.pushed_to_default rules.

When the same key appears several times, the strongest tier wins (closing > non-closing > relation). If two places give the same tier, the order branch > title > body > commit decides which source is kept.

Default magic words

Tier Default words and phrases (from src/parse/magicWords.ts)
closing close, closes, closed, closing, fix, fixes, fixed, fixing, resolve, resolves, resolved, resolving, complete, completes, completed, completing, implement, implements, implemented, implementing
non-closing ref, refs, references, part of, contributes to, toward, towards
relation relates to, related to

An instance admin can replace these lists in God mode, under Magic words. Each entry may contain only lowercase letters and single spaces, up to 40 characters. Each tier needs 1–100 entries, and a word may belong to one tier only.

A magic word is followed by an optional colon and then at least one space. Several keys can follow one word, joined by ,, and, & or spaces.

Reference examples

Text Where Result (real parser) Why
WEB-42-checkout-button branch WEB-42 (closing) bare key in a branch
feature/web-42-login branch WEB-42 (closing) branch keys are case-insensitive
WEB-42 Keep the checkout button visible title WEB-42 (closing) bare key in a PR title
web-42 keep the button visible title no reference lowercase bare key in a title

fixes web-42 body WEB-42 (closing) key after a magic word is case-insensitive

see web-40 body no reference lowercase bare key in a body

Fixes WEB-1 & WEB-2 body WEB-1 (closing); WEB-2 (closing) & joins keys
Closes: WEB-42 body WEB-42 (closing) optional colon, then a space
Text Where Result (real parser) Why
Closes:WEB-42 body WEB-42 (relation) no space after the colon: only the bare key counts
Closes WEB-0042 body WEB-42 (closing) leading zeros are normalised
X-42 WEB_42 WEB-42more 42-WEB body no reference not keys
UTF-8 SHA-256 CVE-2024 body no reference deny-listed prefixes
Closes WEB-42⏎skip WEB-42 body skipped: WEB-42 skip removes the key from this parse
Fixes WEB-42⏎ignore WEB-43⏎Fixes WEB-43 body WEB-42 (closing); skipped: WEB-43 ignore works like skip
WEB-42 Move the button commit WEB-42 (relation) bare key in a commit message
Inputs Result (real parser) Why
branch: web-42-checkout
body: Refs WEB-42		 WEB-42 (closing, from branch) branch (closing) beats body Refs (non-closing)
title: Checkout tweaks
body: Refs WEB-42⏎Relates to WEB-42		 WEB-42 (non-closing, from body) non-closing beats relation
title: WEB-NEW Add rate limiting create in: WEB WEB-NEW asks for a new item
title: Tidy styles
body: web-NEW and WEB-new		 create in: WEB only uppercase NEW counts

skip KEY and ignore KEY count only in a pull request body, are case-insensitive and cover one key each. The key is dropped from this parse wherever it appears (branch, title or body), but a link that git-sync already stored is not removed.

WEB-NEW in a title or body asks git-sync to create a new work item in the project whose identifier is WEB. NEW must be uppercase. This happens on the opened, edited and reopened events.

Smart Commit grammar

<anything> KEY [KEY…] <anything> #command [args] #command [args] …

  • Each line of a commit message is read on its own. A line needs at least one key before its first #command.
  • #comment <text> takes the rest of the line as the comment. A #tag or key inside the comment stays text.
  • #time <duration> accepts w, d, h and m units, with decimals; 1w = 5d and 1d = 8h. It is posted as a Plane comment, Time logged: <duration> (<n> minutes).
  • Any other #word is a workflow-state command.
Commit message Result (real parser)
WEB-42 #comment Checked at 320, 375 and 390 px keys WEB-42 · comment “Checked at 320, 375 and 390 px”
Fix layout WEB-42 #time 1h 30m keys WEB-42 · time 1h 30m = 90 min
WEB-42 #time 1w 2d 4h 30m keys WEB-42 · time 1w 2d 4h 30m = 3630 min
WEB-42 #time 1.5h keys WEB-42 · time 1.5h = 90 min
WEB-42 #in-review #time 45m #comment Ready for Sam keys WEB-42 · state #in-review · time 45m = 45 min · comment “Ready for Sam”
WEB-33 WEB-34 #in-progress #comment Shared validation helper keys WEB-33, WEB-34 · state #in-progress · comment “Shared validation helper”
WEB-42 #comment see #12 and WEB-7 — this stays text keys WEB-42 · comment “see #12 and WEB-7 — this stays text”
WEB-42 #time 3x keys WEB-42 · error: #time needs a duration such as 1w 2d 4h 30m, got “3x”
WEB-42 #comment keys WEB-42 · error: #comment has no text
#comment no key before the command nothing runs
Done. #comment WEB-42 after the command nothing runs
WEB-42 updated the docs nothing runs
WEB-42 #done⏎WEB-43 #comment Second line, own key keys WEB-42 · state #done ‖ keys WEB-43 · comment “Second line, own key”
Commit message Result (real parser)
WEB-42⏎#comment key on the line above nothing runs

State commands

A state command is matched against the states of the work item’s own project, in three steps:

  1. The full state name with spaces as hyphens (#in-review).
  2. The same name ignoring hyphens and apostrophes (#inreview).
  3. The leading whole words of exactly one state’s name.

If two states match at the same step, the command is refused as ambiguous. A command never moves an item into a triage state.

States of the example project: Backlog, Todo, In Progress, In Review, In QA, Done, Cancelled.

Command Result (real resolver)
#in-review → In Review
#In-Review → In Review
#inreview → In Review
#done → Done
#todo → Todo
#in-qa → In QA
#in refused: ambiguous
#progress refused: no such state
#cancel refused: no such state
#shipped refused: no such state

Appendix D · Rule reference: triggers, conditions, actions

Each mapping has a list of rules, stored as YAML in versions. Every event is checked against the list from the top. The first rule whose trigger and conditions match is the only one that runs. If no rule matches, nothing happens.

The Rules tab writes this YAML for you: its lifecycle table and branch-aware rules compile to it. You can also edit the YAML directly in Rules (YAML). The yaml and example blocks in this appendix were checked with the real parser (parseRules in src/rules/engine.ts).

- name: Merged into staging moves to QA     # optional, shown in the audit log
  when: pull_request.merged                 # one trigger, or a list of triggers
  if:                                       # optional; every condition must hold
    base_branch: "^staging$"
  then:                                     # one or more actions, run in order
    - set_state: started:In QA

Shipped defaults

A new mapping uses the lifecycle table below until an admin saves something else.

Lifecycle point Trigger Plane state
Branch pushed branch.created started:In Progress
Draft PR opened pull_request.drafted started:In Progress
PR opened / ready for review pull_request.opened started:In Progress
Review requested pull_request.review_requested started:In Review
Merged (base branch matches ^main$) pull_request.merged completed:Done
Lifecycle point Trigger Plane state
Changes requested, approved, ready for merge, closed without merge, reopened — no change

Triggers

Trigger When it fires Which work items it acts on
pull_request.drafted A PR is opened as a draft or converted to draft Items linked to the PR
pull_request.opened A PR is opened, or a draft is marked ready for review Items linked to the PR
pull_request.review_requested A reviewer is requested Items linked to the PR
pull_request.changes_requested A review asks for changes Items linked to the PR
pull_request.approved A review approves, but the PR is not yet ready for merge Items linked to the PR
pull_request.ready_for_merge The PR is open and not a draft, has at least one standing approval and no standing change request, and all checks and statuses passed. Fires once per head commit. Items linked to the PR
pull_request.merged The PR is merged Items linked to the PR (merge guard applies)
pull_request.closed_unmerged The PR is closed without merging Items linked to the PR
pull_request.reopened The PR is reopened Items linked to the PR
pull_request.* Any of the above —
branch.created The first push of a new branch (not the default branch, not a revert-… branch) Keys in the branch name; finished or cancelled items are never moved back
push Any push Keys in the branch name and commit messages
commit.pushed_to_default A push to the repository’s default branch Keys in the commit messages
Trigger When it fires Which work items it acts on
check_suite.<conclusion>, e.g. check_suite.success, check_suite.failure A check suite completes; check_suite.* matches all Items linked to the PR of the checked commit
deployment_status.<state>, e.g. deployment_status.success A deployment status is reported; deployment_status.* matches all Items linked to the PR of the deployed commit
issue.<action>, e.g. issue.closed, issue.labeled An event on a mirrored issue (GitHub or Plane) The mirrored work item
comment.<action>, e.g. comment.created A comment on a mirrored issue or linked PR The mirrored or linked work item

Conditions (if:)

Key Value Matches when
base_branch regular expression The PR’s target branch matches, for example ^main$ or ^release/
head_branch regular expression The source branch matches, for example ^hotfix/
labels_any list of label names The GitHub object has at least one of the labels
labels_all list of label names It has all of the labels
author login or list The GitHub user who caused the event (case-insensitive)
repo owner/name or list The repository (case-insensitive)
project Plane project ID or list The work item’s project (exact)

An event that has no value for a condition, such as a push with no base branch, does not match a rule that needs it.

Actions (then:)

Action Example Effect in Plane
set_state set_state: started:In Review Moves the item. The target is group:Name, a group alone (completed), or a state name. If the name is missing but the group has exactly one state, that state is used.
add_label / remove_label add_label: needs-qa Adds or removes a project label; a missing label is created
assign assign: sam-reviews Assigns the Plane member linked to that GitHub login
comment comment: "Deployed to {{deployment.environment}}" Adds a comment
add_link add_link: {url: "{{deployment.url}}", title: Staging} Adds a link
log_time log_time: 30m Adds the comment Time logged: 30m (Plane CE has no time tracking)
create_issue create_issue: {project: WEB, title: "Follow up {{issue.title}}"} Creates one new item in that project (ID or identifier only)

Text values can use {{…}} placeholders from the event:

  • deployment.environment and deployment.url for deployment triggers.
  • issue.number, issue.title and issue.url for issue.* and comment.* triggers.
  • comment.body and comment.url for comment.* triggers.

If a placeholder is missing, the rule fails and the failure is written to the audit log.

Tier gating

How strongly a work item is linked limits only set_state:

  • Relation links never change state.
  • Non-closing links (Refs WEB-41) change state on every trigger except pull_request.merged.
  • Closing links change state on merge only when at least one linked PR merged and no linked PR is still open. A PR that cannot be read counts as open. This merge guard is checked only at the moment of the merge.

All other actions run for every tier.

Examples

Branch-aware delivery (staging first, then main):

- name: Merged into staging moves to QA
  when: pull_request.merged
  if: {base_branch: "^staging$"}
  then: [{set_state: "started:In QA"}]
- name: Merged into main is done
  when: pull_request.merged
  if: {base_branch: "^main$"}
  then: [{set_state: "completed:Done"}]

Note a failing build and a deployment on the work item:

- when: check_suite.failure
  then: [{add_label: build-failing}, {comment: "CI failed on this work item's pull request."}]
- when: deployment_status.success
  if: {head_branch: "^release/"}
  then: [{add_link: {url: "{{deployment.url}}", title: "Release candidate"}}]

Hotfixes skip review:

- when: [pull_request.opened, pull_request.drafted]
  if: {head_branch: "^hotfix/", labels_any: [urgent]}
  then: [{set_state: "started:In Review"}, {assign: jordan-acme}]

Note: Saving YAML replaces the whole list, including the defaults. Copy the default rules you still want into your YAML, or build the rules with the lifecycle table, which compiles them for you.

Appendix E · Known limitations and defects

This appendix lists what git-sync does not do in this release, and the defects found while writing this manual. Each limitation was checked in the code. Where older documents said otherwise, the code wins. The evidence is in manual/notes/discrepancies.md.

Limitations by design or not yet built

Limitation What to do instead Evidence
Time is a comment only. #time posts Time logged: <duration> (<n> minutes), and the rule action log_time posts Time logged: <duration>. Plane CE has no time tracking to write to. Read the comments, or keep time in another tool src/github/smart-commits.ts, src/github/pr-automation.ts
Plane-side changes are authored by the bot. Smart Commit comments, rule changes and mirrored edits in Plane show the git-sync service account. The commit’s GitHub login appears in the comment (“via 3b2335d by alex-dev”). Connect your GitHub account anyway: changes you make in Plane then reach GitHub as you, and git-sync can recognize you D-07
The signed-commit checkbox is not enforced. God mode’s Require signed commits for Smart Commits is saved and shown, but the push handler reads only the environment variable. Set REQUIRE_VERIFIED_COMMITS=true in git-sync.env and restart git-sync D-01, src/app/push.ts
GitHub autolink references are unavailable. The option is shown disabled. Keys in GitHub text are still linked by the Development panel and link-back comments Workspace.tsx
The branch name template cannot be edited. It is always {key}-{title-slug}, which can also use {username}. — D-09
The Development panel has no commit list. It shows pull requests, builds, deployments, previews and branches. Open the branch or PR on GitHub DevPanel.tsx
Limitation What to do instead Evidence
Previews come only from deployments. A deployment URL on *.vercel.app, *.netlify.app, *.pages.dev or *.amplifyapp.com becomes a preview. A Markdown “… Preview” link in a PR body is not detected. Have your host report a GitHub deployment D-11
Commit messages never link a pull request. Only the branch name, title and body do. Put the key in the branch or PR title D-06
The merge guard is checked once. If WEB-36 has two PRs and one merges while the other is open, the item stays put. Closing the other PR later does not move it. Move the item by hand, or merge the last PR D-08
Deleting a Plane item does not close the GitHub issue. Plane v1.4.2 sends no delete webhook. Reconciliation (hourly by default) marks the link orphaned and comments on GitHub; archived items are recorded silently. Close the GitHub issue yourself D-15
Comment edits and deletions are not mirrored. Only new comments are copied. Post a follow-up comment src/sync/mirror.ts
Unmapped GitHub assignees are dropped, not guessed. Unmapped @mentions become links to the GitHub profile. Link every member under User links D-16
Never synced: priority, dates, estimates, cycles, modules, parent and sub-items, relations, attachments, pages, views and pull requests (PRs are never mirrored as issues). — Chapter 13
Limitation What to do instead Evidence
Members cannot see the GitHub Sync menu. In Plane, Workspace settings → GitHub Sync is for admins only. Members open /git-sync/ui/workspaces/<slug>/account directly packages/constants/src/settings/workspace.ts
The audit log has no filter controls. Filters work only as URL parameters (?errors=1, ?mappingId=, ?hours=). Use the Errors in the last 24 hours link, or edit the URL D-12
Saving YAML replaces the default rules. Keep the defaults in your YAML, or use the lifecycle table Appendix D
The review-requested default needs an In Review state. If the project has no In Review state but has several started states, the rule fails and the failure is audited. Add an In Review state in the Started group D-20
The Plane request-rate setup check can say “Needs attention”. It compares git-sync’s active client limit with PLANE_API_RATE_PER_MINUTE. Plane CE v1.4.2 does not report its own limit, so git-sync cannot verify Plane’s API_KEY_RATE_LIMIT. Keep PLANE_API_RATE_PER_MINUTE equal to Plane’s API_KEY_RATE_LIMIT, then restart git-sync src/ui/setup-check.ts
Installer wording. install.sh --help says “adds Git Sync to Plane’s menus”, but the menu is labelled GitHub Sync. — D-22

Defect found while making this manual

  1. The link-back comment for a WEB-NEW pull request shows the project, not the new key. When a PR titled WEB-NEW Add rate limiting to the sign-up form created WEB-46 in the demo run, git-sync commented on GitHub:

    Linked Plane work item:
- WEB: http://plane.example.com/acme/projects/…/issues/…

    The comment should say WEB-46. The link URL is correct; only the label is wrong. The cause is that createRequested in src/app/pr.ts (around line 167) passes the project identifier as the item’s identifier. Found in the demo run; text in manual/notes/demo-output/README.md.

When git-sync changes, rebuild the manual. If a later release changes a screen or a rule, the code is the authority: check it with npm run manual:verify.

Where the pictures come from

Every image caption starts with its source:

  • Screenshot (test Plane) and Screenshot (GitHub) were captured for the developer handbook from the running test Plane CE v1.4.2 and the public GitHub pages of the test repository (docs/handbook/HANDBOOK_NOTES.md).
  • Screenshot (demo instance) was captured for this manual from the real git-sync service code and user interface, run locally:
    • It uses a throwaway in-memory PostgreSQL database (PGlite), seeded with the Acme / Website demo data.
    • Only the two network edges are stand-ins: a small in-memory Plane API and an in-memory GitHub API (manual/demo/server.ts).
    • Every page, button, message, audit entry and Development-panel row in these pictures was produced by git-sync’s own code from realistic webhook deliveries. The deliveries were signed and sent through the real webhook endpoints, then processed by the real handlers and the ordered outbox.
    • No real Plane, GitHub account or production system was touched.
  • Diagram and Illustration are drawings. An Illustration stands in for a screen that could not be captured.
  • [[SCREENSHOT NEEDED]] marks a screen that needs a signed-in browser that was not available, such as GitHub’s own forms or a Plane work item showing the Development section. Each placeholder names the capture command for later.

All screenshots are redacted before capture: email addresses, IP addresses, tokens, long IDs, the App slug, the Client ID and personal avatars are hidden or replaced. Orange numbered callouts match the numbered steps in the text.

Rebuilding

From the repository root, on the docs/user-manual branch:

npm ci
npm run manual:all          # seed the demo instance, capture, build and verify
# or step by step:
npm run manual:seed         # start the demo instance with its seed data
npm run manual:capture      # all screenshots; add: -- --only <id>
npm run manual:build        # dist/git-sync-user-manual.pdf, .html and cheat-sheet.pdf
npm run manual:verify       # labels, grammar tables, secrets, links, coverage

Playwright, Chromium and markdown-it are installed with npm i --no-save, so package.json and the lock file do not change. The grammar tables are regenerated by manual/scripts/grammar-tables.mjs from the real parsers. manual/scripts/check-labels.mjs checks that every bold UI label appears in the source code or in a verified capture.
